shots.narration: Every PayPal dispute costs a small seller time and money. And now there's a new kind: the buyer's AI assistant ordered the wrong size.
This is Rebuttal. Normally a PayPal webhook starts it; here I click Analyze.
It only reads: the dispute from PayPal, plus the order, tracking and store policies.
The buyer says she asked for a medium. Her assistant, Atlas, was told the same, and ordered a large.
The store shipped exactly what was ordered, to the right address. Every one of these facts is computed in code, not guessed by a model.
Now the decision. The baseline reasoner's first instinct is a free replacement, which would keep the sale.
shots.scriptText: Now the decision. The model's first instinct is a free replacement, which would keep the sale.

shots.narration: But PayPal only allows refund offers on this dispute. The guard catches that and proposes a full refund once the return is scanned, and the message promises the right item.
I add a line in my own words, then approve.
Before anything leaves, it shows the exact PayPal call: make offer, refund with return, forty-eight dollars, with my wording.
One click. The audit trail records my approval and the single write.
In AG Studio, the merchant sees what disputes cost, what was kept and what was refunded, and whether the guard changed the model's pick.
Why trust it? Only one step in the app can write to PayPal, and it won't run without a human approval.
Analysis runs on a read-only client, and tests scan the code for any other route to a write.
On two sets of ten disputes written blind to the code, the model alone got seven right each time. With the guard, ten and nine.
On the twenty we tuned on, rules alone solve one of four hard cases. The model with the guard solves all four.
This part is real. A buyer filed a dispute in the PayPal sandbox, a signed webhook reached Render, and the agent stopped at the approval gate. Nothing was written to PayPal.
Rebuttal is for the shop with no dispute team: the agent digs, the merchant decides.
This recording used a mock of PayPal's sandbox. Sandbox only: no live money.
